constraints.summary: Keep v1 and v2 client contracts backward-compatible during transition
constraints.scope: payments API request/response shapes exposed to internal services and docs
constraints.gate: wait_for:payments-client@2.x published and v1 client still supported
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Deploy schema/serializer changes before code that depends on them
constraints.scope: pydantic model rewrites, field serializers, orm-mode replacements, and any new response fields
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Maintain a dual-write/dual-serialize window until all consumers migrate
constraints.scope: OpenAPI output, JSON payload serialization, and any response fields that changed under Pydantic v2
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Do not introduce breaking schema changes before mobile SDK is in users' hands
constraints.scope: any request/response schema change that affects mobile clients
constraints.gate: wait_for:new mobile SDK shipped to app stores and in user hands
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Preserve current validation behavior for accepted request bodies unless explicitly loosened
constraints.scope: Pydantic v2 stricter coercion on charge/payment request models
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Run schema diff checks before publishing v2 JSON/OpenAPI
constraints.scope: Regenerated OpenAPI schema, TypeScript client v2, mobile SDK schema, and downstream event payloads
constraints.rollback: Do not publish the new schema artifacts; revert generated outputs to v1 and keep existing client versions

constraints.summary: Keep any payload-shape changes backward compatible during transition
constraints.scope: Response JSON fields consumed by Snowflake feeds and any stored/evented payment payloads
constraints.rollback: Revert serialization changes to the prior JSON shape and republish the v1-compatible artifacts

constraints.summary: Schedule any DB migrations or backfills outside business hours
constraints.scope: Any schema or data backfill needed to support model serialization or persisted payload changes
constraints.rollback: Stop the migration job and restore from the latest pre-change snapshot or backup

constraints.summary: Throttle backfills to preserve IOPS and replica lag budget
constraints.scope: Historical backfills or reprocessing caused by new serialized fields or stored JSON rewrites
constraints.rollback: Pause the backfill, reduce batch size, or restore the last consistent checkpoint

constraints.summary: Delay dropping legacy columns until the quiet period passes
constraints.scope: Any old columns/tables retained for v1-v2 coexistence during the mixed-fleet transition
constraints.rollback: Recreate the dropped column/table from backup or keep the legacy storage path in place

constraints.summary: Stage canary with feature flag and keep v1 rollback ready
constraints.scope: payments-api migration from FastAPI 0.95.2/Pydantic v1 to FastAPI 0.110/Pydantic v2
constraints.rollback: flip the rollout flag back to v1 behavior; redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Hold promotion until canary is stable for 24h
constraints.scope: advance from canary to wider production rollout for payments-api
constraints.gate: wait_for:24h stable canary with no error-budget burn
constraints.rollback: reduce traffic to the previous deployment slice and keep the flag on v1

constraints.summary: No production cutover during incident windows or Friday afternoon
constraints.scope: all deploy, canary promotion, and client/server schema publish steps
constraints.gate: window:Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 local time, outside incident freeze
constraints.rollback: pause rollout and retain current production version

constraints.summary: Do not advance if p99 validation latency regresses materially
constraints.scope: /v1/payments/charge and other high-volume validation paths during rollout
constraints.rollback: route traffic back to v1 deployment and disable v2 flag

constraints.summary: Approve v2 validation parity review before prod cutover
constraints.scope: Pydantic v2 coercion changes, validators, and any relaxed strict=False fields
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Complete SOC2 control evidence update for new validation path
constraints.scope: Migration evidence covering validation rules, bypass risk review, and test results
constraints.rollback: pause rollout and revert to previous validated release

constraints.summary: Notify partners before any externally visible schema/client change
constraints.scope: OpenAPI regeneration, docs.acme.internal/payments, and @acme/payments-client@2.x release
constraints.rollback: withhold client v2 publish and redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Preserve audit trail coverage during dual-version transition
constraints.scope: Period where v1 and v2 clients are both supported and server behavior may differ
constraints.rollback: disable v2 rollout and restore prior request logging/audit hooks

constraints.summary: Notify partner integrators before any breaking schema change
constraints.scope: OpenAPI/schema changes affecting docs.acme.internal/payments and client contracts
constraints.rollback: revert to prior public schema/client release and suspend rollout

constraints.summary: Give internal service consumers advance notice of client v2
constraints.scope: @acme/payments-client major version publication and downstream consumer migration
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Do not roll during launch windows or major customer events
constraints.scope: Production cutover for payments-api, SDK publication, and schema release
constraints.gate: window:outside launch windows and major customer events
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Support and escalation owners must be staffed for the rollout
constraints.scope: Production rollout period and first customer-facing release window
constraints.gate: approval:Support lead and named escalation owner
constraints.rollback: halt rollout and revert to prior release version

constraints.summary: Keep v1 and v2 client/schema compatibility during migration
constraints.scope: OpenAPI regeneration, published @acme/payments-client major version, server response/request shapes
constraints.gate: wait_for:all critical endpoints validated against both v1 and v2 client test suites
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Allow a dual-support window for @acme/payments-client 1.x
constraints.scope: Server-side API behavior while internal services migrate off client 1.x
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Ship a compatibility shim for old and new request/response parsing
constraints.scope: payments-api deploy path, especially request validation and response serialization
constraints.gate: wait_for:shim regression tests passing for legacy .dict()/.json() consumers
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Block cutover until rollback to FastAPI/Pydantic v1 is verified
constraints.scope: production rollout and staged deployment plan
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

constraints.summary: Have a fallback if new API publish slips past consumer migration
constraints.scope: release sequencing for server cutover vs client 2.x adoption
constraints.rollback: redeploy_previous

final_plan.summary: Migrate FastAPI/Pydantic with staged compatibility, schema review, dual-support, and gated production cutover.

steps.action: Run inventory and codemod dry-run: apply bump-pydantic across the repo, enumerate validator/root_validator, encoders, orm_mode, dict/json, and schema-affecting models.
steps.observability: Codemod diff size, list of touched models/routes, count of remaining v1 APIs

steps.action: Manually rewrite the 6 root validators, 3 json_encoders to field_serializer, orm_mode models to ConfigDict(from_attributes=True), and replace .dict()/.json() call sites that codemod missed.
steps.rollback: revert model and serializer changes to last known good commit
steps.observability: Unit test failures, serializer output diffs, model validation regressions

steps.action: Characterize Pydantic v2 coercion changes on charge/payment request models, add explicit strict=False only where approved, and fix validator ordering/async-validator replacements for the 2 tax-service endpoints.
steps.rollback: restore prior validation logic and remove newly relaxed fields
steps.observability: Validation rejection rate, payload samples that now fail, tax-service call success/error rates

steps.action: Prepare compatibility shim and regression suite for legacy .dict()/.json() consumers, then verify request/response parsing works for both old and new client expectations.
steps.gate: wait_for:shim regression tests passing for legacy .dict()/.json() consumers
steps.rollback: disable shim path and revert parsing/serialization compatibility changes
steps.observability: Shim test pass rate, parsed payload equivalence, serialization round-trip diffs

steps.action: Generate the v2 OpenAPI schema, run schema diff checks, and validate critical endpoints against both v1 and v2 client test suites.
steps.rollback: do not publish the new schema artifacts; revert generated outputs to v1 and keep existing client versions
steps.observability: Schema diff report, endpoint test matrix, breaking-change candidates

steps.action: Publish the new major TypeScript client @acme/payments-client@2.x and regenerate the mobile SDK from the approved schema diff.
steps.rollback: withhold client v2 publish and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Package publish success, SDK generation success, consumer notice delivery status

steps.action: Run partner-integrator and internal consumer comms for the new schema/client, then wait for mobile SDK to be shipped to app stores and in users' hands before any breaking server-side schema change.
steps.rollback: revert to prior public schema/client release and suspend rollout
steps.observability: Notice date, app store release status, rollout/installation telemetry

steps.action: Deploy the compatibility server release behind a feature flag with both v1 and v2 serialization paths enabled, keeping response shapes backward compatible during the transition.
steps.rollback: flip the rollout flag back to v1 behavior; redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Canary error rate, validation rejection rate, response-shape parity, p99 validation latency

steps.action: Promote canary to wider production only after 24h stable canary, security approval, SRE rollback verification, and support/escalation staffing are in place.
steps.gate: wait_for:24h stable canary with no error-budget burn
steps.rollback: reduce traffic to the previous deployment slice and keep the flag on v1
steps.observability: Error-budget burn, canary stability, SRE approval status, support coverage, p99 latency

steps.action: Complete SOC2 evidence update and post-cutover monitoring, then keep dual-support active for at least 8 weeks while tracking consumer migration and downstream parse errors.
steps.rollback: pause rollout and revert to previous validated release
steps.observability: SOC2 review completion, downstream parse errors, consumer migration coverage, audit trail coverage

conflicts.issue: BackendOwner wants v1/v2 contract compatibility during transition, while ProductPM requires partner notice before externally visible schema/client changes; resolved by sequencing comms before publish and keeping compatibility during rollout.

BackendOwner wants dual-serialize support until consumers migrate, while ConsumerSubsystem requires a minimum 8-week dual-support window; resolved by maintaining dual support after v2 publish and before any retirement.

BackendOwner wants schema/serializer changes deployed before dependent code, while SRE requires gated canary and rollback-ready rollout; resolved by doing code/schema prep first, then canary under feature flag.

DataPlatform requires schema diff approval before publishing v2 JSON/OpenAPI, while ProductPM requires partner notice before schema/client changes; resolved by diff review first, then notice, then publish.

DataPlatform wants off-peak maintenance windows and throttled backfills, while SRE wants Mon-Thu daytime canary/promotion without incidents; resolved by avoiding backfills in cutover and limiting rollout to approved windows.

Security requires SOC2 evidence completion and approval for validation parity, while ProductPM requires staffing and launch-window avoidance for release timing; resolved by finishing security review before production promotion.

Security requires audit/trust review of relaxed validation paths, while ConsumerSubsystem requires a dual-support window and rollback verification; resolved by keeping dual-support while security validates parity and audit coverage.

ProductPM requires internal consumer notice before client v2 publication, while ConsumerSubsystem requires maintaining old client support for 8 weeks after publish; resolved by notice first, publish second, then long dual-support.
